runner.selector.title: Select test tasks

runner.capability.audio: Can you hear the Access Link sounds during this run?

runner.setup.missing: The test environment is missing or incomplete and will now be set up.
runner.setup.network: Matching tools and plugins are reused; downloads occur only for missing or changed pinned versions.
runner.setup.ruff: Checking Ruff and installing it when needed.
runner.setup.clangTidy: Checking Clang-Tidy and installing it when needed.
runner.setup.markdownlint: Checking markdownlint-cli2 and installing it when needed.

runner.setup.pyrightIntegrity: The Pyright archive SHA-512 check failed. Expected: {0}; found: {1}

runner.setup.toolProbes: Checking the real output of every required linter against its test fixture.
runner.setup.toolProbeFailed: Direct tool probe failed for {0} (exit code {1}).

runner.clean.confirm: Really remove the isolated test state under tmp/?

runner.pluginMissing: The installed Neovim Access Link plugin was not found at {0}. Install local components from the NVDA menu first or use -AccessLinkPlugin.
runner.pluginMismatch: The installed Neovim plugin does not match the current repository. Expected runtime code: {0}; installed: {1}. Reinstall local components from the NVDA menu and restart the test.
runner.notApplicable: This task is omitted automatically because this equipment is unavailable: {0}
runner.launchPrompt: Ready? Press Enter to start only this task in Neovim.
runner.orientation: Neovim will replace the PowerShell view in the SAME original Windows Terminal tab. This is intentional. Your normal Neovim configuration is not used.
runner.claimReminder: In Neovim: first press Escape once. Enable Access Link from the NVDA menu if needed, focus this original terminal tab, and press F12 exactly once. Answer Yes if asked to remember the binding and wait briefly for the connection; switching windows must not be necessary.
runner.controls: Unsure what to do? Press Escape, then F2: Neovim displays and Access Link speaks the test ID, purpose, steps, and pass condition again. Only after the described check, press Escape and F10 to return here to PowerShell.
runner.afterReturn: You are back in PowerShell in the original Windows Terminal tab. Assess only the task you just performed.
runner.note: Short reason without private paths, account names, or other secrets
runner.resume.none: There is no incomplete run below tmp/human-test-results/ yet. Start a new test first.
runner.resume.retry: Should previously blocked or skipped tasks be reopened as pending?
runner.resume.reopened: {0} task(s) were reopened. Tasks already passed or failed remain unchanged.
runner.complete: The run has ended. Machine verification follows.
runner.verifyPrompt: Path to the JSON result file
runner.dryRun: Dry run completed; the runner and Neovim configuration are technically startable.
runner.noPendingSteps: This test area has no pending applicable tasks.
runner.interrupted: Progress remains saved and can be resumed from the start menu.

plan.lspNative.title: Native LSP and completion workflow
plan.lspNative.description: Checks LSP status, parameter help, native completion, search, and multi-file changes with real NVDA output.
plan.lspNative.status.title: Report the active LSP clearly
plan.lspNative.status.purpose: Checks whether Access Link clearly identifies the language server active for the Python file. LSP is the interface through which Neovim receives language features such as completion and rename.
plan.lspNative.status.action:
1. F3: query the active language server.
2. Wait for the complete announcement.
3. Escape, then F10: end the test without saving.
plan.lspNative.status.expected: NVDA reports that Pyright is active for the Python buffer. It does not speak Lua tables or protocol data.
plan.lspNative.automaticParameters.title: Track the active parameter while typing
plan.lspNative.automaticParameters.purpo: Checks whether NVDA automatically identifies the parameter being edited while typing and moving back, without disrupting input or Braille output.
plan.lspNative.automaticParameters.actio:
1. F3: open a prepared empty calculate_total() call and enter Insert mode.
2. Wait for the first parameter announcement; then slowly type 3.5, 2, 0.1 and pause briefly after each comma.
3. Press Ctrl+Left three times: move from the third argument through the second to the first.
4. Within the first argument, press Left and then Right; observe speech and, if available, Braille.
5. Escape, then F10: end the test without saving.
plan.lspNative.automaticParameters.expec: NVDA announces price, quantity, and discount in order, then price again when moving back. Left or Right within the same argument remains silent. Hints follow without disruptive delay; the source text remains on Braille.
plan.lspNative.parameters.title: Hold function parameters on Braille
plan.lspNative.parameters.purpose: Checks the held parameter view: signatures and individual parameters should be readable on a physical Braille display without moving the real Neovim cursor.
plan.lspNative.parameters.action:
1. Hold NVDA, briefly press Space, and release only Space: open the signature view.
2. Keep NVDA held; use the Braille display's forward/back controls to page through signature 1 and return to its start.
3. Press l three times: show parameters 1, 2, and 3.
4. Press j, then l twice: switch to signature 2 and show its parameters 1 and 2.
5. Press k, then l: show signature 1 and its parameter 1 again. Then press j, followed by h: show signature 2 and, despite moving backward, its parameter 1.
6. Release NVDA and repeat the held query once without moving the cursor.
7. Press F4, perform the held query, and release NVDA; then press F4 and perform it again. F4 places the cursor first on the opening and then on the closing parenthesis.
8. Escape, then F10: end the test without saving.
plan.lspNative.parameters.expected: Speech and Braille show complete signatures, documentation, and the price, quantity, and discount parameters. On Braille, S, P, and D identify signature, parameter, and documentation. j/k changes signatures; after each change, h/l starts at parameter 1. Releasing NVDA restores the source text; queries on the function name and both parentheses do not move the real cursor.
plan.lspNative.completion.title: Operate and perceive native completion
plan.lspNative.completion.purpose: Checks Neovim's built-in LSP completion: suggestions should be spoken clearly, selected safely, and accompanied by suitable menu open and close sounds.
plan.lspNative.completion.action:
1. F3: open the prepared completion position and enter Insert mode.
2. Before F5, press Ctrl+N once; neither text nor menu should change.
3. F5: open the suggestion menu.
4. Use Ctrl+N to move beyond calculate_total, calculate_tax, and calculate_tip to the state with no selection and then back to the first suggestion. Move back at least once with Ctrl+P.
5. Ctrl+Y: accept a function; then read the line and cursor character. With audio, listen for one distinct open and close sound.
6. Escape, then F10: end the test without saving.
plan.lspNative.completion.expected: Before F5, Ctrl+N has no effect. After F5, NVDA announces every selected suggestion and the state with no selection. Acceptance responds smoothly, inserts exactly one pair of parentheses, and places the cursor between them. With audio, opening and closing sound once each; selection changes remain silent.
plan.lspNative.searchReplacement.title: Search and replace with native Neovim commands
plan.lspNative.searchReplacement.purpose: Checks search and replacement across multiple files. Quickfix is Neovim's result list: it collects matches so they can be read in sequence without manually opening every file.
plan.lspNative.searchReplacement.action:
1. Slowly type /calculate_tip, observe search previews, then press Enter and n once.
2. F3: start the prepared project search and open its Quickfix result list.
3. Press F4 three times: move forward to the last result; press F4 again: test the last boundary.
4. Press F5 three times: move backward to the first result; press F5 again: test the first boundary.
5. F6: start replacement. Wait for each prompt, then press y for the first, n for the second, and a for all remaining matches.
6. Escape, then F10: end the test without saving.
plan.lspNative.searchReplacement.expecte: Slash search reports useful previews and then the match. F3 announces the result count. F4 and F5 read complete result rows and both boundaries without file or focus announcements. Every replacement prompt appears before input with its line and position. Finally, NVDA gives exactly one aggregate count of changed and unsaved buffers.
plan.lspNative.rename.title: Rename a symbol through the native LSP workflow
plan.lspNative.rename.purpose: Checks LSP rename: Pyright should change a function name in its definition and all loaded references together; Access Link should report only the verified result.
plan.lspNative.rename.action:
1. F3: open an empty name field. Enter calculate_gratuity and press Enter.
2. Wait for the completion announcement.
3. Press F4 twice: first read the changed import row, then the changed call row.
4. Escape, then F10: end the test without saving.
plan.lspNative.rename.expected: NVDA announces once that two buffers changed and remain unsaved. No internal text, cursor, or focus changes are announced first. The two F4 reports identify reference 1 of 2 and 2 of 2 with calculate_gratuity; the current buffer remains unchanged.
plan.lspNative.bufferReplacement.title: Replace across loaded buffers
plan.lspNative.bufferReplacement.purpose: Checks Neovim's native buffer-list replacement: two loaded files should change together without announcing internal buffer visits separately.
plan.lspNative.bufferReplacement.action:
1. F3: start the prepared bufdo replacement across both loaded Python buffers.
2. Wait for the completion announcement.
3. Press F4 twice: report each file that was verifiably changed.
4. Escape, then F10: end the test without saving.
plan.lspNative.bufferReplacement.expecte: NVDA announces exactly once that two buffers changed and two remain unsaved, without preceding file, focus, text, or cursor reports. The two F4 reports name lsp_features.py and lsp_rename_consumer.py with two occurrences of calculate_tip_buffered each.
plan.diagnostics.title: Diagnostic output and earcons
plan.diagnostics.description: Checks Ruff warnings and errors with speech, navigation, sounds, and held Braille output.
plan.diagnostics.navigation.title: Speak, navigate, and perceive diagnostics
plan.diagnostics.navigation.purpose: Checks diagnostics, meaning warnings and errors from an analysis tool at specific code positions. NVDA should read Ruff messages in full, navigate forward and backward, and use suitable sounds.
plan.diagnostics.navigation.action:
1. F6: run Ruff; wait for “Diagnostics ready”. The cursor is then on the first test diagnostic.
2. F7: read the diagnostic at the cursor.
3. Repeatedly press F9: move forward through every diagnostic to the Ruff F821 error for missing_name and then back to the first.
4. F8: move backward to the last diagnostic. With audio, compare warning and error sounds.
5. F5: query a prepared clean position.
6. Escape, then F10: end the test without saving.
plan.diagnostics.navigation.expected: F7 reads the first F401 warning. F9 reaches every numbered diagnostic and wraps from the last to the first; F8 moves backward to the last. Each key press produces exactly one complete message. With audio, warning, error, and the F5 “no diagnostic” result use three clearly distinct sounds; together with completion, the run covers five sounds.
plan.diagnostics.held.title: Hold a diagnostic on Braille
plan.diagnostics.held.purpose: Checks whether multiple diagnostics on the same code row can be held on a physical Braille display and read individually.
plan.diagnostics.held.action:
1. F6: run Ruff; wait for “Diagnostics ready”. Then press F7.
2. Hold NVDA and Shift, briefly press Space, then release only Space and Shift. Keep NVDA held.
3. j: move from the F401 diagnostic for path to sep. k: return to path.
4. Release NVDA.
5. Escape, then F10: end the test without saving.
plan.diagnostics.held.expected: The F401 diagnostics for path and sep are fully readable on Braille and change with j/k. Releasing NVDA restores the previous Braille output.
plan.focus.title: Focus isolation and fail-open behavior
plan.focus.description: Checks with two real Windows Terminal tabs that Access Link affects only the connected Neovim session.
plan.focus.workflow.title: Distinguish claimed and unclaimed terminal tabs
plan.focus.workflow.purpose: Checks fail-open behavior: an unconnected tab must behave like a normal NVDA terminal. After Neovim exits, the same must immediately be true for the previously connected tab.
plan.focus.workflow.action:
1. In the test Neovim, press Escape, connect the original tab with F12, and leave Neovim open.
2. Use the plus button or profile menu to open a second Windows Terminal tab with PowerShell. Do not start Neovim or press F12 there.
3. In the second tab, check ordinary input and navigation without submitting a command.
4. Return to the original tab; press Escape, then F10.
5. In the restored PowerShell view, check ordinary input and navigation again.
plan.focus.workflow.expected: The second unclaimed tab keeps NVDA's normal terminal behavior and receives no Neovim output from the first tab. After F10, PowerShell in the original tab is immediately usable normally as well; no Braille output is stuck and input is not blocked.
plan.nvimCmp.title: Optional nvim-cmp compatibility
plan.nvimCmp.description: Checks operation and NVDA output of the optional nvim-cmp completion plugin.
plan.nvimCmp.menu.title: Operate and perceive nvim-cmp suggestions
plan.nvimCmp.menu.purpose: Checks whether Access Link presents nvim-cmp's suggestion list as clearly as Neovim's built-in completion. nvim-cmp is an optional completion plugin.
plan.nvimCmp.menu.action:
1. F3: open the prepared completion position and enter Insert mode.
2. Before F5, press Ctrl+N once; neither text nor menu should change.
3. F5: open the nvim-cmp menu.
4. Use Ctrl+N to reach calculate_total, calculate_tax, and calculate_tip; move back with Ctrl+P.
5. Ctrl+Y: accept a function; then read the line and cursor character. With audio, listen for one open and one close sound.
6. Escape, then F10: end the test without saving.
plan.nvimCmp.menu.expected: Before F5, Ctrl+N has no effect. After F5, NVDA clearly announces nvim-cmp suggestions; navigation and acceptance respond smoothly. In the test configuration, the function gains exactly one pair of parentheses and the cursor is between them. With audio, opening and closing sound once each; selection changes remain silent.
plan.blinkCmp.title: Optional blink.cmp compatibility
plan.blinkCmp.description: Checks operation and NVDA output of the optional blink.cmp completion plugin.
plan.blinkCmp.menu.title: Operate and perceive blink.cmp suggestions
plan.blinkCmp.menu.purpose: Checks whether Access Link clearly presents blink.cmp's suggestion list. blink.cmp is an optional plugin for fast completion suggestions.
plan.blinkCmp.menu.action:
1. F3: open the prepared completion position and enter Insert mode.
2. Before F5, press Ctrl+N once; neither text nor menu should change.
3. F5: open the blink.cmp menu.
4. Use Ctrl+N to reach calculate_total, calculate_tax, and calculate_tip; move back with Ctrl+P.
5. Ctrl+Y: accept a function; then read the line and cursor character. With audio, listen for one open and one close sound.
6. Escape, then F10: end the test without saving.
plan.blinkCmp.menu.expected: Before F5, Ctrl+N has no effect. After F5, NVDA clearly announces blink.cmp suggestions; navigation and acceptance respond smoothly. Blink's auto-brackets insert exactly one pair of parentheses and place the cursor between them. With audio, opening and closing sound once each; selection changes remain silent.
plan.cDiagnostics.title: C diagnostic with Clang-Tidy
plan.cDiagnostics.description: Checks real Clang-Tidy C errors through nvim-lint with speech, navigation, and sound.
plan.cDiagnostics.presentation.title: Perceive a Clang-Tidy diagnostic
plan.cDiagnostics.presentation.purpose: Checks whether Access Link also presents C diagnostics clearly. Clang-Tidy analyzes the C code; nvim-lint passes its findings to Neovim.
plan.cDiagnostics.presentation.action:
1. F2: repeat the task; it must begin with test ID D3.
2. F6: run Clang-Tidy; wait for “Diagnostics ready”.
3. F7: read the missing_first error as the first diagnostic.
4. F9: move to missing_second; press F9 again: wrap to the first diagnostic.
5. F8: move backward to missing_second again. With audio, listen for the error sound.
6. Escape, then F10: end the test without saving.
plan.cDiagnostics.presentation.expected: F2 announces D3. F7 reports missing_first as 1 of 2. F9 reaches missing_second as 2 of 2 and then 1 of 2 again; F8 moves backward to 2 of 2. Each diagnostic appears exactly once per key press and, with audio, produces exactly one error sound.
plan.markdownDiagnostics.title: Markdown diagnostic with markdownlint
plan.markdownDiagnostics.description: Checks a real markdownlint warning through nvim-lint with speech and sound.
plan.markdownDiagnostics.presentation.pu: Checks whether Access Link also presents Markdown findings clearly. markdownlint detects a second level-one heading here; nvim-lint passes the warning to Neovim.
plan.markdownDiagnostics.presentation.ac:
1. F6: run markdownlint; wait for “Diagnostics ready”.
2. F7: read the warning at the current position.
3. F9: reach the same single warning again as a navigation target. With audio, listen for the warning sound.
4. Escape, then F10: end the test without saving.
plan.markdownDiagnostics.presentation.ex: F6 announces collection and readiness without inserting a single character such as “number sign”. F7 and F9 each report the markdownlint MD025 warning once with a meaningful position. With audio, each message produces one warning sound.
plan.lazy.title: Plugin management with lazy.nvim
plan.lazy.description: Checks the lazy.nvim window plus install, update, and sync with fully isolated local test plugins.
plan.lazy.window.title: Read and operate the lazy.nvim window
plan.lazy.window.purpose: Checks whether Access Link recognizes lazy.nvim as a plugin manager and makes its line-oriented interface understandable.
plan.lazy.window.action:
1. F3: open lazy.nvim. The complete command bar must be spoken. To read it again, hold NVDA and explore its lines with k and j; the Neovim cursor must not move.
2. Without NVDA, use j and k to read several plugin rows; speech reports collapsed and Braille shows +.
3. Enter: open details; speech reports expanded and Braille changes to - without a transient message. Press Enter again: speech reports collapsed and Braille changes to +.
4. ?: open and close help. Then q and F10: end the test.
plan.lazy.window.expected: NVDA speaks the complete command bar when opening; line exploration reads it again without moving the Neovim cursor. Plugin rows contain the name and spoken state. Expanding or collapsing changes the Braille marker without a transient Braille message; stale, duplicate, or unrelated file and focus announcements remain absent.
plan.lazy.install.title: Install a test plugin
plan.lazy.install.purpose: Checks clear feedback for a real lazy.nvim install from an isolated local Git repository.
plan.lazy.install.action:
1. F3: open lazy.nvim and read the missing access-link-install-target entry.
2. F4: start installation; wait for the completion announcement.
3. F5: verify the test plugin's actual Git state.
4. q: close lazy.nvim. Then F10: end the test without saving.
plan.lazy.install.expected: NVDA announces the start and end of installation once each without inferring success from the completion report. F5 confirms that access-link-install-target is completely installed at the expected revision; no user data or real plugins are changed.
plan.lazy.update.title: Update a test plugin
plan.lazy.update.purpose: Checks clear feedback for a real lazy.nvim update between two local Git revisions.
plan.lazy.update.action:
1. F3: open lazy.nvim and read access-link-update-target with its available update.
2. F4: start the update; wait for the completion announcement.
3. F5: verify the test plugin's actual Git state.
4. q: close lazy.nvim. Then F10: end the test without saving.
plan.lazy.update.expected: NVDA announces the start and end of the update once each without inferring success from the completion report. F5 confirms the new expected Git revision; no user data or real plugins are changed.
plan.lazy.sync.title: Synchronize install, update, and cleanup
plan.lazy.sync.purpose: Checks lazy.nvim synchronization as one coherent operation with a missing, an outdated, and a no-longer-configured test plugin.
plan.lazy.sync.action:
1. F3: open lazy.nvim and read the prepared plugin states.
2. F4: start synchronization; wait for the completion announcement.
3. F5: verify installation, update, and removal from the actual Git directories.
4. q: close lazy.nvim. Then F10: end the test without saving.
plan.lazy.sync.expected: NVDA announces synchronization as one operation with exactly one start and one completion message; internal install, update, and cleanup steps cause no extra flood of messages. F5 confirms all three expected final states.
